response.text:
TREC’s 2025 recommendation task distinguishes substitutes by shared function and complements by added functionality; compatibility and subjective preference are separate questions. Its 2026 overview reports 15.1% of assessed pairs as “unable-to-assess,” supporting explicit uncertainty labels. Substitute relationships alone do not establish redundancy: browsing alternatives, replacing equipment, and purchasing another copy can reflect different intentions. Co-occurrence likewise does not prove complementarity or compatibility. [TREC task definitions](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html), [2025 track overview](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.17138v1).

Suggested diagnostic adaptation: annotate relation type, compatibility status, and evidence sufficiency separately, citing exact title/description spans. Mark conflicts only when explicit specifications contradict; missing connectors, dimensions, editions, or device models mean “unknown.” Use histories and timestamps as behavioral context, without inferring ownership, fulfilled demand, or purchase intent. Audit a small sample stratified across all four categories, predicted relations, and missing-information cases with two independent human annotators and adjudication; report agreement, assessed coverage, and error among assessed cases. Treat substitute concentration as potential redundancy and complements as potentially useful, pending intent and compatibility evidence. Abstention research supports evaluating coverage alongside conditional error; confidence requires validation rather than acceptance at face value. These are proposed probes, not measured results, and should supplement the fixed HR@10 evaluation. [Abstention survey, 2025](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/), [uncertainty-based abstention, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10960).
